RoomType.rationale: FlyconidNormal.RoomType => RoomType.Monster (FlyconidNormal.cs:17). Sim carries no room_type field on the Encounter dataclass; 'flyconid' is placed in rooms.py:101's normal_keys for _overgrowth_rooms() (seam/rooms_and_map owns the picker itself). GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) matches EncounterModel.cs:70/89's Monster=>10/20 defaults, which FlyconidNormal does not override.

Tags.rationale: FlyconidNormal.Tags => [EncounterTag.Mushroom, EncounterTag.Slimes] (FlyconidNormal.cs:19-23). Not modeled on the sim's Encounter dataclass itself; instead rooms.py:115 (_overgrowth_rooms's tags dict, the sim's counterpart to ActModel.AddWithoutRepeatingTags's tag-safe picker) carries tags['flyconid']=('mushroom','slimes') -- same two tags. _shares_tags (rooms.py:237-240) compares as an unordered set intersection, matching Tags.Intersect(other.Tags).Any() (EncounterModel.cs:279-286), so tag ORDER is immaterial on both sides. This is the run-layer picker's mechanism (seam/rooms_and_map, out of scope for this record beyond confirming the transcription is correct).

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: No sim counterpart. C#'s AllPossibleMonsters getter (FlyconidNormal.cs:25-40) builds [Flyconid, LeafSlimeM, TwigSlimeM] (Flyconid first, then _mediumSlimes in order) purely for ActModel.AllMonsters (ActModel.cs:169, read only by ModelDb.Monsters -> UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68/147's dev-console 'monsters' listing and NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164's stats-screen ratio label) and the Bestiary screen (NBestiary.cs:194) -- all UI/dev-console, zero gameplay or RNG effect, confirmed by reading every caller in src/. The headless sim has neither surface, so omitting a counterpart costs nothing observable.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: FlyconidNormal.GenerateMonsters (FlyconidNormal.cs:42-49) returns a 2-array whose element[0] is `(base.Rng.NextItem(_mediumSlimes).ToMutable(), null)` and element[1] is `(ModelDb.Monster<Flyconid>().ToMutable(), null)` -- C# evaluates array initializers in source order, so the ONE draw over _mediumSlimes=[LeafSlimeM,TwigSlimeM] happens BEFORE the Flyconid is appended, and the slime is first in the returned list. flyconid.py:91-99's parity branch (selection_rng is not None) does exactly this: `slime_cls = selection_rng.next_item([LeafSlimeM, TwigSlimeM])` then `return [slime_cls(hooks, rng), Flyconid(hooks, rng)]` -- same order [LeafSlimeM,TwigSlimeM], same draw count (1), same draw-before-Flyconid-construction order, no slot names on either side. This verdict covers roster/order/slot/draw-count/draw-order for the PARITY code path only; the non-parity fallback (selection_rng is None) is filed separately below as it draws from the wrong stream, not the wrong count/order.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: (structural -- Encounter dataclass has no hook methods)
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by FlyconidNormal. The sim's Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) declares no hook methods and is never passed to HookSystem.register -- it is plain data, structurally incapable of joining the hook walk, which reproduces 'the encounter itself is not a listener' exactly.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward gold ladder (the encounter brief's 5th thing to verdict)
guards.rationale: FlyconidNormal does not override MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, so both inherit EncounterModel.cs:64-100's RoomType ladder (Monster=10-20) times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under AscensionLevel.Poverty. FLYCONID_NORMAL carries min_gold=None, max_gold=None (Encounter dataclass default, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so rewards.py:886-887 falls back to GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) -- the same ladder. Ascension (Poverty) scaling is out of scope by the audit contract (rewards.py:32's explicit 'no Scarcity/Poverty scaling').

guards.what: EncounterModel.Rng independence (per the encounter brief: verify the sim does not draw encounter rolls off a shared/run-level stream) -- shared mechanism id encounter/_selection_rng_fallback
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `RunState.create_combat` now builds the per-encounter Rng on BOTH paths: with a string seed from `rng_set.seed` as before, and without one from a run seed derived at construction (`run.derive_encounter_seed`, a hash of the shared generator's STATE, so it consumes no draw and shifts no other legacy stream). `create_monsters`' `selection_rng=None` arm is therefore unreachable from any production call site, and the composition no longer moves when the shared stream does — executed in test/test_encounter_selection_rng.py (test_the_composition_does_not_move_with_the_shared_stream) and by audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py legacy-shared-stream.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: FlyconidEncounter.create_monsters (flyconid.py:91-99) only draws its NextItem-equivalent from an isolated stream when `selection_rng is not None`. `selection_rng` is `RunState.create_combat`'s `encounter_selection_rng` (run.py:1609-1613), which stays None unless `self.rng_set is not None` -- and `self.rng_set` is only set when RunState is constructed with a `string_seed` (RunState.__init__). run_env.py's RunState construction (the RL training path, `RunState(rng=self._rng, character=self._character)`, run_env.py:747) never passes one, so EVERY training episode falls into flyconid.py:98's else branch: `slime_cls = rng.choice([LeafSlimeM, TwigSlimeM])` on `self._rng` -- the SAME per-combat random.Random every other unseeded draw in the fight uses (monster HP rolls, the Flyconid's own move_ai branch picks, etc.), not an isolated stream. This directly contradicts EncounterModel.cs:42-45's documented guarantee ('independently of the run's centralized RNG... safe... because we don't need to keep track of a given encounter's RNG state once it's over') for exactly the reason the guarantee exists: consuming the roster draw off the shared stream shifts every subsequent unseeded draw in the combat relative to a hypothetical isolated-stream draw, and it composes with every other draw made off self._rng before or after this one. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e1.py flyconid-selection-rng` prints the gating chain and the create_monsters source live. Impact: any non-parity combat (i.e. every RL training episode and every CombatState built without an explicit rng_set) that reaches a Flyconid fight has its composition draw entangled with the rest of the fight's unseeded randomness -- not observable against a game fixture (parity mode, which all conformance tests use, is unaffected and correctly isolated via make_encounter_rng), but real for the sim's own internal determinism/reproducibility guarantees. Same shape as `two_tailed_rats/G2` (batch e8, not yet filed under a shared id as of this writing) -- propose unifying under `encounter/_selection_rng_fallback`; every create_monsters override across underdocks/hive/overgrowth that takes a `selection_rng=None` default parameter (bowlbugs, corpse_slug, decimillipede, ruby_raiders, scroll_of_biting, slimes, slithering_strangler, two_tailed_rat, plus this unit) shares the identical gating shape and should be swept rather than re-derived per unit.
